body_long:
Saint-Barth opens its 2026–27 season with five new names in about a month, from late October to late November. None of them is a new building. Two are icons changing hands or changing skin, three are restaurant brands landing on the island.

## Airelles Le Guanahani

Since 1 November 2026, the former Rosewood Le Guanahani is Airelles Le Guanahani, the tenth Maison of Airelles and its first in the Caribbean. Rosewood's management ended on 1 October. The resort, owned by Stéphane Courbit's LOV Group, sits on a private peninsula of about seven hectares with two beaches inside a protected nature reserve. It has 66 keys (29 rooms, 28 suites and 9 signature suites), 20 of them with a private pool, two restaurants including La Table du Guanahani and The Grill, three bars and an Airelles Spa developed with Laboratoires Botanique Avancée. Anne-Laure Ollagnon is CEO of Airelles.

## Le Sereno

Le Sereno, on the lagoon of Grand Cul-de-Sac, reopens on 16 November 2026 after a three-year project. Its owners, Luis and Angelica Contreras, have had every accommodation redone, with canopies and furniture designed by Patricia Urquiola. The new Suite des Pêcheurs covers 230 square metres with a private pool and its own gate to the beach. BOKAO, a new beach club, opens on an adjoining property, and the Italian restaurant Le Sereno Al Mare has been redesigned. Rates are announced from €1,550 to €18,600 a night. Carlos de la Barra was appointed general manager at the turn of the year, after posts at Bulgari, One&Only Palmilla and Rosewood Villa Magna.

## Langosteria at Cheval Blanc St-Barth

Langosteria opened on Flamands beach, at Cheval Blanc St-Barth, on 22 October 2026. It is the first address outside Europe for the Milanese seafood house founded in 2007 by Enrico Buonocore, and its second collaboration with Cheval Blanc after Paris. Christelle Hilpron is general manager of Cheval Blanc St-Barth.

## Loulou at Fouquet's Saint-Barth

Loulou, the Parisian table of the Tuileries, Ramatuelle and Courchevel, opens on Shell Beach in November 2026, in the former Shellona space, as the beach restaurant of Fouquet's Saint-Barth. The Barrière hotel, formerly Le Carl Gustaf, became the fourth Fouquet's in 2026. Its general manager is Enrique Glückmann.

## Zuma Saint-Barth

Zuma makes its Caribbean debut in Gustavia, at 19 Rue de la République, overlooking the harbour. Its website announces an opening on 20 November 2026; some press reports give 25 November. The restaurant is seasonal, until April 2027, with three kitchens (main kitchen, sushi counter and robata grill) and resident DJs. Sven Koch is CEO of Azumi, the group behind Zuma.

## Why it matters

On Saint-Barth, this season's new names do not build. They take over a hotel, or a table inside one. The owners who stay, like the Contreras family at Le Sereno, answer with a three-year renovation.
